project_type: Python AWS Lambda functions for AI agent game (AWS AI League turtle maze)
language: Python 3.12 (invoke tests with python3, not python)
build_system: No build system - pure Python lambdas, no packaging step
test_framework: unittest - tests in tests/test_agent.py, uses _invoke() helper that calls lambda_handler(event, None) directly and json-parses the returned body
build_command: python3 -c 'import memoryquestion; import pathfinding; import codeexecutor; import webscraper; print("OK")'
verification_instructions: Run python3 -m unittest discover tests/ and confirm all tests pass. Baseline is 108 tests, all passing.
setup_instructions: No setup needed. Python 3.12 available. No network required - all tests run offline with inline fixtures.
environment_constraints: Network mode is restricted (offline). No external network calls in tests. Do NOT push or open PRs - orchestrator handles publishing. Work stays on branch fix/c3-memory-map-recall.
contribution_requirements: No formal CONTRIBUTING.md. Follow existing patterns. Do NOT modify door/key logic (transform rules, key/door routing) - the red/green door fix is already merged on main and must stay untouched. CHANGELOG.md uses versioned entries (currently at v9); add a new v10 entry at the top.
key_patterns: Each lambda has lambda_handler(event, context) returning {'statusCode': int, 'body': json_string}. Events can have a 'body' key (API Gateway style, possibly a JSON string) or be a direct dict. memoryquestion.py has a module-level _memory_store = {} dict that persists across warm invocations (i.e. for one game session). Actions: count, store, retrieve, transform. store/retrieve/transform use _memory_store; count currently recomputes from a passed-in game_map and does NOT use _memory_store. _handle_count uses ID_PATTERN (\bc(\d+)\b) to find challenge IDs in the question and Counter to tally cells. _err(code, msg) helper for error responses. pathfinding.py receives the full game_map at game start and is the one place the map is reliably seen.
directory_structure: Flat repo: lambda .py files at root, per-tool system prompts as *_system_prompt.txt, supervisor_system_prompt.txt, tests/test_agent.py with inline fixtures, CHANGELOG.md, .agents/tasks/ with prior task folders.
